caveat: REAL Craft CMS booted per version via composer (craftcms/cms 5.8.20/5.8.22/5.8.23) + MariaDB + real `php craft install` + the PUBLIC GraphQL schema opened (via Craft's own service layer, pcb_setup.php) to the asset-upload mutation. The attacker drives Craft's OWN `save_pcbvol_Asset(_file:{url})` mutation over EXTERNAL HTTP; Craft's OWN validateHostname()/handleUpload()/validateIp() run inside the app. NOTHING is source-lifted. The IPv4-only-resolver blind spot is real: a dual-stack Docker net (192.0.0.0/24 + fd00:ec2::/64, enable_ipv6) + a static UDP DNS sidecar answer host6.pcb.test A=NODATA + AAAA=fd00:ec2::254, so Craft's gethostbyname misses the AAAA while its Guzzle/libcurl connects over IPv6. The prior faithful-core harness.php lift is RETIRED (files left in dir per no-rm, no longer built/served).

audit.evidence: Real Docker build (php:8.3-cli + composer craftcms/cms 5.8.20/5.8.22/5.8.23 + MariaDB 11, 3 real-Craft images + static UDP DNS sidecar + dual-stack canary on 192.0.0.0/24 + fd00:ec2::/64). In-container versions verified: v0=5.8.20 v1=5.8.22 v2=5.8.23. External HTTP trigger: POST /index.php?p=actions/graphql/api save_pcbvol_Asset(_file:{url}) server-side Guzzle SSRF. Observed 5-way differential on real Craft: seed http://seed.pcb.test/flag (IPv4 metadata) -> flag@v0, blocked@v1 ('contains an invalid hostname'), blocked@v2 ('resolves to an invalid IP address'); residual http://host6.pcb.test/flag (A NODATA, AAAA-only fd00:ec2::254) -> flag@v1 via real IPv6 connect (primary_ip=fd00:ec2::254), blocked@v2 ('resolves to an invalid IP address'). Gate passed. Primitive check: v1 gethostbyname('host6.pcb.test')='host6.pcb.test'; v1 curl [fd00:ec2::254] returns flag.

root_cause: SSRF via IPv6-only DNS resolution: the CVE-2025-68437 fix validates hosts with the IPv4-only gethostbyname(), so an AAAA-only host defeats the cloud-metadata IP blocklist and the fetch connects over IPv6 (CWE-918)

v0.ref: src/gql/resolvers/mutations/Asset.php handleUpload(): `$this->createGuzzleClient()->request('GET', $url, ['sink' => $tempPath])` fetches `_file.url` with NO host validation (CVE-2025-68437)

v1.ref: CVE-2025-68437 fix = validateHostname($url): parse host, hex-normalize octets, require FILTER_VALIDATE_DOMAIN & reject IP literals, reject a metadata-hostname list, then `gethostbyname($host)` and reject a cloud-metadata IPv4 blocklist (169.254.169.254/170.2, 100.100.100.200, 192.0.0.192). gethostbyname() is IPv4-ONLY: for an AAAA-only host it returns the hostname STRING (never in the numeric blocklist) so the guard passes, then Guzzle/libcurl resolves the AAAA and connects over IPv6 to the metadata endpoint. No request-time IP check in 5.8.22. (fix introduced 5.8.21 commit 013db63, IPv4 blocklist added 5.8.22)

v2.ref: CVE-2026-27129 fix commit 2825388b4f32fb1c9bd709027a1a1fd192d709a3: validateIp() gains a cloud-metadata IPv6 PREFIX blocklist (fd00:ec2::, fd20:ce::, ::1, fe80:, ::ffff:) evaluated via str_starts_with against the ACTUAL connected primary_ip (the RequestOptions::ON_STATS request-time hook added by the sibling CVE-2026-27127 fix, commit a4cf3fb). The IPv6-only host's real connect to fd00:ec2::254 is rejected.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The SSRF validation in Craft CMS's GraphQL Asset mutation uses gethostbyname(), which only resolves IPv4 addresses. When a hostname has only AAAA (IPv6) records, the function returns the hostname string itself, causing the blocklist comparison to always fail and completely bypassing SSRF protection. This is a bypass of the security fix for CVE-2025-68437 (GHSA-x27p-wfqw-hfcc).
